data.name: Ansu
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Ansu is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Anus’, which means ‘drop’ or ‘sweat’. This name is believed to be associated with Lord Indra, the God of Rain, Thunder, and Lightning. In Hindu scriptures, Anus is mentioned as the sweat droplets that fall from the God Indra's body while he is engrossed in his divine duties.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ansu holds great significance in Hindu culture, especially in relation to agriculture and rain. As a derivative of Lord Indra, the Rain God, Ansu embodies the power and importance of rain in our lives. In many regions of India, this name is given to boys born during the rainy season, as a tribute to the blessings of Indra.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Ansu signifies the eternal divine grace and presence of Lord Indra, whose blessings ensure the growth of crops and the sustenance of life. It is a constant reminder of our dependence on the divine providence for our very existence and the need to cultivate a deep sense of gratitude towards the divine powers. By bearing this name, an individual may be encouraged to live in harmony with nature, respecting and preserving its abundant resources while upholding the values of compassion, love, and wisdom.

historical_references.reference: Ansu is a Sanskrit name which appears in the ancient Hindu scriptures, the Mahabharata and the Ramayana. It is the name of a divine river that flows from the heavenly realm to the earth, providing sustenance and nourishment to all living beings.
Ansu was also the name of a ruler of the Vedic civilization in ancient India, around 1500 BCE. He was a king of the Solar Dynasty, known for his wisdom and just rule.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Ansu continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
